title: Ephemeral KV shadow tracing and adaptive slab reclamation policy prototype
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Summary: We observe gradual resident GPU memory growth in workloads with aggressive continuous batching + KV prefetch. Unlike classic slab bloat caused by long-lived pinned staging, this growth appears correlated with ephemeral KV shadow allocations created during interleaved prefetch windows and not fully reclaimed due to race conditions in slab coalescence and stream synchronization. Scope: reproduce across multi-stream inference with mixed sequence lengths, continuous batching enabled, and KV prefetch ON. Goals: 1) build fine-grained ephemeral allocation traces tied to logical KV keys/requests, 2) prototype an adaptive slab reclamation policy that drains candidate slabs when ephemeral residue crosses thresholds, 3) validate performance regressions (latency p95/p99), and 4) propose safe rollout path (feature flag + telemetry).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reproducer that reliably produces >10% resident growth in <6 hours on our stress cluster with current default prefetch settings. 2) Ephemeral KV shadow traces that map allocation -> key_id -> stream_id with timestamps, queryable in internal trace UI. 3) Prototype reclamation toggled via runtime flag that reduces residual resident memory by at least 30% in the reproducer without increasing p99 latency >5%. 4) Design doc with rollback plan and telemetry for rollout.
reproducer_steps: 1) Checkout branch: mem/kv-ephemeral-trace (WIP). 2) Deploy to internal stress cluster (g4dn-sim nodes) with continuous_batching=true, kv_prefetch_window=64, kv_prefetch_parallel=4. 3) Run mixed-seq stress harness: 60% short (<128), 40% long (>1024) for 6 hours. 4) Observe resident RSS, cudaMemPool stats, and stream-epoch logs. 5) Query ephemeral-trace API for leaked entries. Expected: steady upward RSS and increasing count of ephemeral shadows not cleaned after stream epoch advance.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hunch: cudaMallocAsync deferred free path may be racing with our slab coalescer worker, leaving small residual pockets (sub-page fragments) referenced by ephemeral bookkeeping.
- Trace instrumentation added to patch: record allocation origin (kv_key hash), allocator slab id, stream id, and epoch at alloc/free.
- Early traces show clusters of allocations from same kv_key across streams where free races with coalescer trim. These allocations transition to 'orphaned' state when the stream that created the KV rotates out of active epoch before coalescer finishes coalescing.
- Sampling of cudaMemPoolDump shows many small freed segments still counted as resident due to outstanding deferred frees in other streams.
- Hypothesis: coalescer backoff timing too long when system under load, allowing ephemeral shadows accumulate beyond internal hysteresis thresholds.
- Experimented with reducing coalescer backoff from 500ms -> 100ms: improved reclamation but increased CPU contention on coalescer worker (measured with perf events).
experiments:
- Trace build: mem/kv-ephemeral-trace (branch). Ran 3 trials of reproducer with and without trace. Observed 32% median reduction in visible orphan count when coalescer backoff shortened, but CPU usage on management threads increased ~18%.
- Prototype adaptive policy: mark slabs with >X% ephemeral orphan ratio and schedule aggressive trim. In 4/5 runs, resident memory dropped 28% vs baseline after 2 hours. Side effect: slight increase in short-tail latency under heavy batch mixes.
- Tried eager cudaFreeAsync draining on completion of KV invalidate operations; reduced orphan lifetimes but caused immediate contention spikes and occasional transient CUDA error 700 on stress nodes. Reverted.
proposed_changes: 1) Ship ephemeral tracing as a gated telemetry-only feature to gather broader data. 2) Implement adaptive slab reclamation heuristic: track ephemeral residue per slab, once a slab crosses configurable threshold, prioritize it for coalescer fast-path; limit rate to avoid CPU runaway. 3) Add coalescer backoff dynamic scaling based on queue depth and CPU headroom. 4) Safety: feature flag + rollout to dedicated pools first. 5) Add acceptance tests to stress harness and synthetic unit harness to validate no p99 regressions.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Faster reclamation reduces memory but increases CPU and possibly contention on allocator metadata, which could worsen latency for high-concurrency workloads.
- Eager draining risks surfacing CUDA driver edge cases; prior attempt triggered error 700 under extreme contention.
- Heuristic tuning may be workload specific; need telemetry and defaults that work across typical customer mixes.
- Complexity: additional per-slab bookkeeping increases allocator state; must ensure low overhead when disabled.
open_questions:
- What threshold value for ephemeral-orphan ratio balances memory recovery and CPU cost? (Need experiments across 5 cluster shapes)
- Is driver-level tuning (cudaMemPoolAttr) available to accelerate deferred free reclamation without application-level workarounds?
- Can we correlate orphan patterns to particular model/kernel combos (attn pattern) to prefer model-aware reclamation?
next_steps:
- [ ] Finish trace integration and enable telemetry-only rollout to canary pools (by 2026-03-05).
- [ ] Run grid of experiments varying threshold, backoff windows, and limiters (by 2026-03-08).
- [ ] Open RFC for adaptive reclamation policy with perf/latency tradeoffs (by 2026-03-10).
- [ ] Implement guarded fast-path coalescer scheduling in runtime and iterate (by 2026-03-15).
